# VRFLog

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/interaction/physics-hold/Runtime/Scripts/Logging/VRFLog.cs#L99)

The framework's log bus. [`Util`](/api/vrframework-core-runtime/Util) pushes every VRF log line through here on its way
to the Unity console; anything that wants to collect them - the VRF Logger window, an in-game
overlay, a file writer - subscribes to [`Emitted`](/api/vrframework-core-runtime/VRFLog#emitted).
Nothing is built when there are no listeners, so this is free in a shipped build.

```csharp
public static class VRFLog
```

## Fields

### CaptureStackTraces {#capturestacktraces}

Whether a managed stack trace is captured per line. Walking the stack is the expensive part
of logging, so it is on in the editor and off everywhere else.


### Forwarding {#forwarding}

True while [`Util`](/api/vrframework-core-runtime/Util) is handing a line to [`Debug`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Debug.html). A collector that
also listens to the Unity console uses this to skip lines it is already receiving here.
